title: Canonical vendor identity registry
description: The single source of truth for VENDOR IDENTITY on this platform. Consumed by platform/lib/vendor_identity.py (the resolver) and mirrored into the vendor_id enum of platform/schema/receipt.schema.json (parity asserted by platform/lib/test_vendor_identity.py, so the two layers cannot drift). Kept as DATA rather than as branches in code so the alias set can be audited and extended without touching the resolver.
relationship_to_councilspec_schema: platform/schema/councilspec.schema.json:442-444 ALREADY constrains participant vendor to a 9-value enum [anthropic, openai, google, meta, mistral, xai, local, human, other]. That prior art is the reason this fix is a superset rather than a new vocabulary: every one of those 9 values resolves here, so the council plane, the receipt plane and the predicate now share ONE identity plane. test_vendor_identity.py asserts the superset relation, so adding a value to the councilspec enum without registering it here fails the suite.
closes_defect: DEFECT D1 - completion-predicate condition 9 accepted 10/10 same-vendor ALIAS pairs as cross-vendor because platform/lib/completion_predicate.py compared free text with ==. Measured by platform/architecture/_probe_crossvendor_alias_hole.py before the fix: 'CONFIRMED HOLE: 10/10 same-vendor alias pairs are accepted as cross-vendor.'

normalize: NFKC-fold the string, then delete every character in Unicode category Cc (control) or Cf (format) - Cf is what makes 'anthropic<U+200B>' and 'anth<U+00AD>ropic' the same token as 'anthropic'
strip ALL leading/trailing Unicode whitespace (this is what closed the 'anthropic ' trailing-space leak)
collapse any internal run of whitespace, '_' or '-' to a single '-'

build LOOKUP CANDIDATES from that key and try them EXACT-FIRST (see `normalization.candidate_order`): the key itself, then its dot-to-dash form, then with a `normalization.domain_suffixes` entry removed, then with `normalization.punctuation_folded_to_separator` characters folded to a separator, and after each of those the same form with trailing `normalization.legal_entity_suffix_tokens` / `normalization.descriptor_suffix_tokens` removed
look each candidate up in the alias index built from `identities[].id` + `identities[].aliases`; the FIRST hit wins and an empty candidate is discarded
resolution_rules.establishes_distinctness: ONLY an identity whose `establishes_distinctness` is true can be one half of a cross-vendor pair. A hosting_substrate or a placeholder names WHERE a model ran or that the field was never filled in - neither is a vendor identity, so distinctness is NOT COMPUTABLE from it and the predicate must return NOT-CHECKED, never SATISFIED.
resolution_rules.unrecognized: A string that resolves to nothing is UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is REJECTED: the predicate returns NOT-CHECKED (which blocks completion) and the schema enum rejects the receipt outright. Treating an unrecognized string as 'distinct because it differs' is precisely the false green D1 records.
resolution_rules.extending: Add an entry (or an alias to an existing entry) here, then re-run platform/lib/test_vendor_identity.py. The receipt-schema parity test will fail until the vendor_id enum in platform/schema/receipt.schema.json is regenerated to match, so the two layers cannot silently diverge.

normalization.why_this_is_data: The resolver READS these lists; it does not branch on them. A real-world vendor spelling is therefore made to resolve by editing THIS FILE and re-running platform/lib/test_vendor_identity.py - no new code path to review. platform/lib/vendor_identity.py falls back to the same defaults when a registry omits this block, so a hand-written test fixture registry still loads.
normalization.candidate_order: EXACT-FIRST, first hit wins: (1) the normalized key, (2) its dot-to-dash form, (3) with a domain suffix removed, (4) with punctuation folded to a separator, and after each of those (5) the same form with trailing corporate/descriptor tokens removed. Exact-first is load-bearing: it is why 'x-ai' resolves to xai instead of being stripped to a bare 'x', and why 'azure-ai' stays the Azure hosting plane instead of folding to a vendor.
normalization.legal_entity_basis: A corporate FORM is not an identity: 'Anthropic PBC', 'OpenAI, Inc.' and 'Google LLC' name the same vendors as 'anthropic', 'openai' and 'google'. Wave 3 measured the cost of not folding them - 3 of the 45 rows in the D1 matrix returned NOT-COMPUTABLE for 'Anthropic PBC', 'Mistral AI' and a zero-width-space variant, so the predicate REFUSED a completion whose reviewer was in fact same-vendor. Refusing is safe (it blocks) but a refusal is not a verdict. Dotted initialisms are listed in their punctuation-folded form ('l-l-c' for 'L.L.C.') because folding runs before suffix stripping.
normalization.descriptor_basis: Generic industry words that sit in a trade name without changing identity ('Mistral AI', 'Cohere Labs', 'Microsoft Research'). Deliberately SHORT. 'cloud' is deliberately NOT here: 'Google Cloud' is a hosting plane that also serves Anthropic models, so folding it to vendor google would recreate D1 in the DANGEROUS direction - it is registered as an alias of the vertex hosting plane instead. Note the asymmetry with 'alibaba-cloud', which IS a vendor alias because Alibaba Cloud is the legal name of the vendor that publishes Qwen. That asymmetry is a decision, not an oversight.
normalization.punctuation_basis: Folded to a separator so 'Anthropic, PBC' and 'Anthropic P.B.C.' reach the same key as 'anthropic-pbc'. '/' and '+' are NOT folded, because two registered placeholder aliases legitimately contain them ('n/a', 'anthropic+openai'). A string that folds to nothing but separators ('!!!', '...') yields an EMPTY candidate, which is discarded - an empty candidate must never match an alias.
normalization.over_fold_guard: Stripping a suffix must never INVENT an identity. Only a TRAILING token from these lists is removed, and only while something remains: 'Acme Inc' -> 'acme' (still UNKNOWN, still a refusal), 'Anthropic Killer Inc' -> 'anthropic-killer' (NOT anthropic), and a bare 'Inc' / 'Ltd.' / 'AI' is never reduced at all. test_vendor_identity.py sweeps EVERY alias in this table through EVERY candidate form and fails if any of them reaches a DIFFERENT canonical id, so a future addition here cannot quietly merge two vendors.
normalization.what_this_does_NOT_do: It does not make an unregistered vendor resolve. An unknown string is still UNKNOWN and still blocks - closing the NOT-COMPUTABLE gap by treating unknown vendors as 'distinct' is precisely the false green D1 records.

alias_exclusions.rule: A HOSTING PLANE IS NOT A VENDOR ALIAS. 'bedrock', 'vertex', 'azure' and 'openrouter' all serve Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models, so folding them into any one vendor would make the gate WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION - it would report a genuinely cross-vendor review as same-vendor and block a valid completion. They are registered below with kind=hosting_substrate and establishes_distinctness=false.
alias_exclusions.parent_and_investor_relationships_are_NO: Corporate ownership is not vendor identity and must never be folded. Microsoft is OpenAI's largest investor and Azure hosts its models, yet ('microsoft', 'openai') is a GENUINE cross-vendor pair that the matrix requires to be SATISFIED - folding on ownership would report it as same-vendor and block a valid completion. The same reasoning excludes 'alphabet' -> google and 'amazon' -> anthropic. Only trade names, product lines, model families, corporate FORM suffixes and spelling variants of the SAME operating vendor are alias grounds.

identities.alias_basis: Product line and model families are the SAME legal vendor. 'anthropic-pbc' is the folded legal name ('Anthropic PBC', 'Anthropic, PBC', 'Anthropic P.B.C.') and is registered EXPLICITLY, not left to the suffix rule, so the receipt-schema enum accepts that spelling at the wire too - the generated enum contains alias-table keys, not resolver candidate forms. 'claude-code' is the CLI, 'opus'/'sonnet'/'haiku' are model families frequently mis-written into a vendor field, 'fable' is the internal codename used in this estate's own docs. Every one of these compared UNEQUAL to 'anthropic' under the pre-fix == gate.

'codex' is OpenAI's coding CLI and is the single most load-bearing alias on this estate: every cross-vendor work unit in the catalog names Codex as the reviewer, and 'openai' vs 'codex' passed the pre-fix gate as CROSS-vendor.
Google DeepMind is Google; Gemini/Bard/PaLM/Gemma are its model lines. NOTE 'vertex'/'vertex-ai' is deliberately NOT here - Vertex AI also serves Anthropic models.

Llama and Code Llama are Meta's model lines. 'meta-platforms' is the trade name in the legal title 'Meta Platforms, Inc.'; it is registered explicitly rather than by adding 'platforms' to the legal-form list, because 'Platforms' is part of the NAME, not a corporate form.

Present in the catalog (4 units declare vendor=mistral). 'mistral-ai' is the vendor's own display name ('Mistral AI', legally 'Mistral AI SAS') and was one of the 3 rows Wave 3 measured as NOT-COMPUTABLE: the table already held 'mistralai' but a SPACE between the words normalizes to 'mistral-ai', which is a different key. Codestral/Devstral/Magistral/Mixtral are Mistral model lines.
Present in the catalog (2 units declare vendor=xai). Grok is xAI's model line.
Vendor plus its model lines.
Qwen/Tongyi are Alibaba Cloud model lines.
Command-R and Aya are Cohere model lines. 'cohere-labs' is the current name of the research arm formerly published as Cohere For AI.
Titan and Nova are Amazon's OWN model lines. 'bedrock' and 'aws' are NOT aliases here - Bedrock is a hosting plane that serves Anthropic and Meta models.
Phi is Microsoft's own model line. 'azure' is NOT an alias - Azure OpenAI Service serves OpenAI models.

A human reviewer does not inherit ANY model vendor's blind spots, so a human/AI pair is genuinely cross-vendor. Present in the corpus: platform/lib/council_protocols/_shared.py:346 emits vendor='human'.

Names WHERE a model ran, not WHOSE model it is. Azure OpenAI Service serves OpenAI models, so 'azure' vs 'openai' is NOT a cross-vendor pair - and it is not provably same-vendor either. NOT COMPUTABLE.

Bedrock serves Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere and Amazon models. 'amazon-web-services' is registered HERE and not on the amazon vendor entry on purpose: it names where a model ran. Registering it makes the refusal precise ('a hosting_substrate, not a vendor identity') instead of the weaker 'not in the registry'. Reading it as a vendor would let an Anthropic-on-Bedrock reviewer pass as cross-vendor against an Anthropic executor.

Vertex AI serves Anthropic models as well as Google's own. Same trap as bedrock. 'google-cloud' and 'gcp' are registered here rather than on the google vendor entry, and this placement is DEFENSIVE: because candidates are tried exact-first, an explicit hosting-plane alias survives even if someone later adds 'cloud' to descriptor_suffix_tokens, which would otherwise fold 'Google Cloud' into vendor google and pass an Anthropic-on-Vertex reviewer as cross-vendor.
A router serves many vendors. The vendor behind a routed call is unknown from this field alone.
Present in the corpus (2 occurrences of vendor='local'). A locally served model is still SOMEONE's model - typically Meta's or Alibaba's - so the substrate name cannot establish vendor distinctness.

Present in the corpus and in the shipped receipt examples: platform/schema/examples/receipt.valid.example.json:103 carries produced_by.vendor='unassigned' while reviewer.vendor='anthropic'. Under the pre-fix == gate that pair read as CROSS-vendor - a second live instance of D1 sitting inside the reference example itself.
44 catalog occurrences. A wildcard is a CONSTRAINT on assignment, not an identity: it cannot be one half of a distinct pair.

Present in the councilspec enum at platform/schema/councilspec.schema.json:444 as the escape hatch. It is NOT an identity: two seats both marked 'other' may be the SAME vendor, so 'other' vs 'other' is not provably same-vendor and 'other' vs 'anthropic' is not provably distinct. NOT COMPUTABLE in both directions.
48 catalog occurrences. 'mixed' names a SET, so it is neither equal to nor distinct from a single vendor. NOT COMPUTABLE.

02.09.2026 P2 (G-1) repair: Cursor is an agent harness that hosts models from several vendors (Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI) the way azure/bedrock/vertex host them; 355 units' emitters name it in reviewer.vendor / produced_by.vendor and became schema-invalid the moment fragment $refs resolved correctly (p2_jsonschema_hook fix). Registered as a hosting substrate, NOT a vendor: a receipt naming Cursor identifies the harness, so it can never be one half of a cross-vendor pair. 'cursor-grok' / 'spacexai-cursor' / 'cursor-grok-4.6' are the harness driving a specific model; they fold to the substrate, and the model vendor must be stated separately where distinctness matters.

02.09.2026 P2 (G-1) repair: ~25 units' emitters name a deterministic re-derivation script (no model) as reviewer.vendor. A script is not a vendor identity, so this is a placeholder kind (NOT-AN-IDENTITY): it can never establish cross-vendor distinctness, which is the conservative reading. Composite tokens that prefix a real vendor ('anthropic-mechanical-...', 'openai-style-cross-probe') are deliberately NOT aliased here - they need the owner's call on whether the vendor or the mechanism is the identity - and probe negative-control tokens ('vendor-x', 'fake-codex', 'planted-catalog-vendor') must stay rejected.
